inputs.text:
An extremely wide, short social banner image, composed specifically for a letterbox strip roughly four times wider than it is tall, with the whole design working inside that narrow horizontal band and nothing important near the very top or bottom edges.

The background is a smooth horizontal gradient running from deep aubergine on the far left through dusty plum in the centre to burnt amber on the far right, overlaid with a subtle fine-grain noise texture.

The left third holds a simple mark: a thin-line outline drawing of a paper aeroplane in pale cream, tilted upward to the right, with a dotted cream trail curving away behind it toward the left edge.

The centre third carries the main text, vertically centred and left-aligned: a headline reading "SLOW MAIL" in a wide cream serif with generous letterspacing, and directly beneath it, at about a third of that size, a subline in pale amber reading "LETTERS THAT TAKE THEIR TIME". Both lines are crisp, correctly spelled and comfortably clear of the top and bottom edges.

The right third holds three small evenly spaced circular badges in outlined cream, each containing a tiny centred icon and a very small label beneath it: a stamp icon labelled "POST", an envelope icon labelled "WRITE", and a clock icon labelled "WAIT". Between the centre text and the badges, a single thin vertical cream rule runs most of the height of the band as a divider.

The layout stays deliberately airy for such a short strip: everything sits on one horizontal axis, no element is cropped by the frame, and the extreme width is used rather than fought.
